title: Evaluate content-addressed compression and differential transport

state.decision_rationale: Rejected as a core MKTCTX feature. Standard transport compression, Git bundles, and content-addressed stores already solve wire and storage reuse; external body references would weaken the packet's standalone model-readable property.

provenance.source_label: Grok design observation: compression and differential story
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Lossless exact chunks are the right default for a source-of-truth packet. A future profile that allows content-addressed or delta-encoded chunks, while still declaring the exact sha256, would make this more practical for repeated or incremental context shipping. When only a few files change, regenerate just those chunks and update the manifest hash rather than shipping a whole new dump.
feedback.normalized_claim: Add a verifiable incremental transport story that reuses content by hash or applies deltas without weakening exact final-content identity.

current_behavior: Each packet is a standalone text artifact containing every non-alias exact or numbered body.
Byte-identical files within one packet are deduplicated through aliases.
No cross-packet content store, external chunk reference, compression wrapper, base-packet link, or delta representation exists.
The optional diff sidecar compares whole previous and current packet text and is not an application format.

proposal.summary: Evaluate separately versioned full, referenced, compressed, and delta transports whose resolved output is still verified by exact file hashes.
candidate_changes: Allow content references by full digest when a declared content store or base packet is available.
Define base packet identity and missing-base failure semantics before adding deltas.
Compare file-level reuse, chunk-level reuse, standard compression, and Git-compatible object transport.
Keep a standalone archival profile that never requires external state.
Treat selective regeneration as creation of a new manifest with explicit references, not mutation of an old immutable packet.
non_goals: Do not call a packet self-contained when required bodies exist only in an undeclared cache.
Do not invent a delta codec before comparing mature compression and Git object reuse.
Do not let transport optimization alter the verified final source hash.

questions: Is the main cost wire size, storage duplication, prompt tokens, or regeneration time?
Who owns and authenticates the referenced content store?
Should deltas operate on files, exact chunks, or canonical compressed blobs?
How many prior packet bases may a consumer need?
Would a Git bundle plus MKTCTX manifest solve transport better than custom deltas?
risks: External references weaken portability and offline use.
Delta chains can become fragile, deep, and expensive to validate.
Compressed or referenced content is not directly model-readable without a materialization step.
Content-store authority introduces security and retention concerns.
evidence_needed: Repeated-packet corpus measuring byte reuse and change frequency.
Size, materialization-time, and complexity comparison across gzip or zstd, Git bundles, content references, and deltas.
Failure fixtures for missing bases, corrupt references, deep chains, and cache eviction.
